hero.headline: US and Iran exchange strikes as ceasefire falters
hero.body:
The United States military conducted strikes against Iranian targets at the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday, prompting Iran to respond with missiles and drones. The exchange represents the most serious test of a month-long ceasefire between the two nations.

The US military said it targeted sites responsible for attacking three American destroyers: the USS Truxtun, USS Rafael Peralta, and USS Mason. According to US Central Command, Iranian forces launched multiple missiles, drones, and small boats at the vessels, though no US assets were struck. The military said it eliminated inbound threats and targeted Iranian military facilities including missile and drone launch sites and command centers.

Iran's military offered a different account, accusing the US of violating the ceasefire by targeting two ships at the Strait of Hormuz and striking civilian areas. The Iranian military spokesperson claimed the US carried out airstrikes on coastal cities including Bandar Khamir and Sirik, as well as the island of Qeshm, which has about 150,000 residents. Iran's armed forces responded by attacking US military vessels, the spokesperson said, claiming to have inflicted significant damage.

President Trump characterized the incident minimally, calling it a "love tap" during an interview with ABC News. "They trifled with us today. We blew them away," Trump told reporters. He insisted the ceasefire remained intact despite the strikes.

On the negotiations front, Trump said a deal "might not happen, but it could happen any day," adding that he believed Iran wanted an agreement more than his administration did. Reports prior to Thursday's exchanges suggested the US and Iran may have been close to a temporary agreement, with a one-page memorandum being shared between Washington and Tehran through Pakistan.

However, senior Iranian officials have recently rejected concessions. Some analysts suggest Iran may prefer to drag out negotiations closer to November's midterm elections in the US, when the Trump administration could face greater pressure to settle the conflict. Regional diplomats warn that Iran risks overplaying its hand, as the current moment offers an opportunity to end the war and claim victory before fighting potentially resumes at a larger scale.

The escalation immediately affected energy markets. Brent crude oil rose to approximately $101 per barrel following news of the attacks. The conflict has already created concerns about fuel costs for American consumers, with rising gas prices becoming a factor in political calculations.

The ceasefire, which had largely held for the previous month, now faces serious questions about its viability. Both sides have accused the other of violations, and despite diplomatic efforts to negotiate an end to the three-month conflict, military operations continue.

cards.headline: Justice Department opens criminal investigation into Trump accuser
cards.teaser: The department is investigating whether E Jean Carroll lied about funding sources for her civil lawsuit against the president.
cards.body:
The US Justice Department has opened a criminal investigation into E. Jean Carroll, the former columnist who accused President Trump of sexual assault. The inquiry examines whether Carroll provided false information regarding the funding she received for her civil lawsuit against Trump.

Carroll previously won her civil case against Trump in court. The new criminal investigation specifically focuses on how she disclosed the financial backing for that legal action.

cards.headline: Cornyn loses Texas primary to Paxton in blowout
cards.teaser: Attorney General Ken Paxton defeated longtime Sen. John Cornyn in the Texas Republican Senate primary.
cards.body:
Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton won the Republican Senate primary against Sen. John Cornyn in a lopsided result that energized President Trump and the MAGA base. The loss dealt a major blow to Senate GOP leaders who had invested tens of millions of dollars in supporting Cornyn.

The outcome puts new pressure on Senate Majority Leader John Thune and other Senate Republicans to align more closely with Trump's agenda. Republican strategists described the result as giving Trump increased leverage over the Senate Republican conference heading into the general election.

cards.headline: White working-class voters turn against Trump
cards.teaser: White voters without college degrees who backed Trump's reelection now disapprove of his job performance.
cards.body:
White voters without college degrees have shifted to net-negative approval of President Trump's job performance, marking a reversal for a demographic that voted to reelect him by a large margin. The group was a core part of Trump's electoral coalition.

The shift represents a significant change in support from a voter bloc that has historically backed Trump by wide margins. The drop in approval comes as multiple challenges face the administration.

cards.headline: Guatemala Agrees to Joint Drug Operations With U.S.
cards.teaser: Guatemala will allow joint military strikes against drug gangs inside its borders.
cards.body:
Guatemala agreed to conduct joint strikes with the United States against drug gangs operating within Guatemalan territory. The agreement is part of a broader Trump administration effort to secure similar arrangements across Latin America.

The deal allows American forces to participate in operations inside Guatemala's borders alongside local authorities. The Trump administration has been pressing multiple Latin American countries to agree to joint operations as part of its approach to combating drug trafficking in the region.

cards.headline: Ebola outbreak in Congo outpaces containment efforts
cards.teaser: An Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo is spreading faster than health workers can contain it.
cards.body:
An Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo is spreading faster than containment efforts can manage, according to the World Health Organization. The WHO's director-general warned that the epidemic is outpacing response operations and urged neighboring countries to take immediate action to prevent the disease from crossing borders.

The Trump administration is building a quarantine and treatment center in Kenya for Americans exposed to the virus, rather than allowing them to return to the United States. Some health experts have criticized this approach, arguing that preventing Americans from coming home may hinder treatment efforts.

cards.headline: CEO confidence drops as Iran war continues
cards.teaser: Business leaders at major companies grew more pessimistic in the second quarter as the Iran conflict extended.
cards.body:
CEO confidence fell 12 points in the second quarter, dropping to 47 on a scale where below 50 indicates more negative than positive sentiment, according to a survey by The Conference Board and The Business Council. The decline reflects ongoing uncertainty as the Iran war continues without resolution.

The conflict has already begun affecting households and businesses. Energy prices have risen significantly due to the war's impact, with typical household energy bills increasing by £221 annually under new price cap regulations. Meanwhile, military escalations continue, with Israel intensifying attacks against Hezbollah in Lebanon and U.S. forces striking Iranian targets as diplomatic negotiations for a ceasefire remain ongoing.

hero.headline: Fire Kills 16 Students at Kenya School
hero.teaser: A fire at a school dormitory killed at least 16 pupils and injured dozens more.
hero.body:
A fire swept through a dormitory at Utumishi Girls Academy in Gilgil, Nakuru county, killing at least 15 students. The blaze occurred overnight at the school, located about 76 miles northeast of Nairobi.

Dozens of other students were injured in the fire. The incident adds to a troubling pattern of deadly school fires that have occurred across Kenya in recent years.

cards.headline: Guatemala Agrees to Joint Drug Operations With U.S.
cards.teaser: Guatemala will allow joint military strikes against drug gangs inside its borders.
cards.body:
Guatemala agreed to conduct joint strikes with the United States against drug gangs operating within Guatemalan territory. The agreement is part of a broader Trump administration effort to secure similar arrangements across Latin America.

The deal allows American forces to participate in operations inside Guatemala's borders alongside local authorities. The Trump administration has been pressing multiple Latin American countries to agree to joint operations as part of its approach to combating drug trafficking in the region.

cards.headline: Russian Fuel Tanker Diverts From Cuba
cards.teaser: A Russian tanker apparently headed to Cuba with fuel changed course, leaving the island without expected supplies.
cards.body:
A Russian tanker that appeared to be traveling to Cuba carrying fuel has changed direction. The development affects Cuba as the island faces fuel shortages under a U.S. oil blockade.

The tanker's diversion represents a setback for Cuba, which has been struggling with energy supply issues. The expected fuel delivery would have provided relief to the island during its current shortage.

cards.headline: Middle East Leaders Reject Trump's Israel Recognition Demand
cards.teaser: Regional analysts say Trump's proposal to require Israel recognition as part of Iran deal has almost no chance of success.
cards.body:
President Trump has proposed requiring more countries to recognize Israel as a condition for resolving the conflict with Iran, building on the Abraham Accords framework that previously normalized relations between Israel and several Arab nations.

Regional analysts and leaders have responded with skepticism to the proposal. Experts assess the likelihood of countries accepting this requirement as extremely low, with observers characterizing the timing and presentation of the demand as perplexing given the current diplomatic landscape in the Middle East.

cards.headline: Justice Department Investigates Trump Accuser E. Jean Carroll
cards.teaser: A criminal investigation examines whether Carroll lied about funding for her civil lawsuit against Trump.
cards.body:
The U.S. Justice Department has opened a criminal investigation into E. Jean Carroll, the writer who accused President Trump of sexual assault. Prosecutors are examining whether Carroll committed perjury during a 2022 deposition in her civil lawsuits against Trump, specifically regarding statements she made about accepting outside financial support for her legal battles.

Carroll, 82, previously won a civil case against Trump. The criminal inquiry marks a significant development in the ongoing legal disputes between the former columnist and the president.

cards.headline: Peter Thiel Establishes Presence in Argentina
cards.teaser: The tech billionaire has developed roots in Argentina, reportedly motivated by concerns about the United States.
cards.body:
Tech billionaire Peter Thiel has established new roots in Argentina. The move is said to be partly motivated by concerns about the future of the United States.

Thiel reportedly shares ideological views with Argentina's right-wing leader. The billionaire's relocation represents a significant geographical shift for one of Silicon Valley's most prominent figures.

cards.headline: War Shapes Street Fashion in Ukraine
cards.teaser: Military-inspired clothing has become widespread in Kyiv as soldiers and civilians show solidarity.
cards.body:
Military-inspired fashion has become visible throughout Kyiv. Both soldiers and civilians have adopted the style, which they describe as a show of solidarity rather than a fashion trend.

The prevalence of military-influenced clothing reflects the ongoing war's impact on daily life in Ukraine's capital. The phenomenon extends across different segments of the population as the conflict continues.

cards.headline: Ohio lawmaker proposes religious heritage curriculum for schools
cards.teaser: A pastor turned state legislator is backing legislation to teach the role of religious values in American history.
cards.body:
An Ohio state lawmaker and former pastor is backing the American Heritage Act, legislation sponsored by Charlie Kirk. The bill would allow schools to teach about the positive influence of Judeo-Christian values in U.S. history.

Critics of the proposal contend it presents a distorted version of American history and would introduce religious perspectives into public school curricula. The debate reflects broader disagreements over how religion should be addressed in educational settings.

cards.headline: Trump budget includes no funding for homeless veterans housing
cards.teaser: The president's budget provides zero dollars for a program he pledged would house 6,000 homeless veterans.
cards.body:
President Trump pledged to house 6,000 homeless veterans, and a related executive order raised hopes among veteran groups that housing efforts would accelerate. However, his budget allocation includes zero funding for this initiative.

Veterans' advocates are questioning why the promised funding has not materialized, pointing to the disconnect between the executive order and actual budget allocation.

cards.headline: Gas tax holiday proposal faces infrastructure funding concerns
cards.teaser: Trump wants to suspend the federal gasoline tax, but the move could drain funds needed for road maintenance.
cards.body:
President Trump is proposing to suspend the federal gasoline tax, which could reduce pump prices by up to 18.4 cents per gallon for drivers nationwide.

The proposal faces significant pushback over infrastructure concerns. The federal gas tax funds roadbuilding and repair projects across the country, but that fund is already experiencing financial strain. Suspending the tax would further reduce available resources for maintaining and improving the nation's roads.

cards.headline: Ousted BP chairman denies misconduct allegations
cards.teaser: Albert Manifold says no one should hide behind anonymity when commenting on his tenure at the energy company.
cards.body:
Former BP chairman Albert Manifold has denied allegations of misconduct following his removal from the role. He characterized the claims against him as false and insisted that critics should not be able to make accusations while remaining anonymous.

BP has declined to comment on whether bullying or overbearing behavior contributed to Manifold's abrupt dismissal from the company.

cards.headline: Democrats see opportunities in Senate races
cards.teaser: The party believes it has chances to win Republican-held Senate seats in upcoming elections.
cards.body:
Democrats are expressing optimism about their prospects in Senate races where Republicans currently hold seats. Party strategists believe they have viable paths to victories that could shift the balance in the chamber.

The confidence comes as both parties prepare for upcoming Senate elections. Democrats are targeting specific GOP-held seats as potential pickup opportunities in their effort to gain seats in the Senate.

hero.headline: Australia Sues 3M for $1.4 Billion Over Forever Chemicals at Military Bases
hero.body:
The Australian government filed a lawsuit against manufacturing giant 3M seeking $1.4 billion in damages, marking the largest lawsuit ever brought by the Australian government.

The case centers on PFAS, a group of synthetic chemicals commonly called forever chemicals because they persist in the environment and human body. Australia alleges that 3M concealed information about the harmful effects of PFAS used at military installations across the country.

PFAS chemicals have been widely used in firefighting foams at military bases for decades. The substances do not break down naturally and can accumulate in soil, water, and living organisms over time.

The Australian government's legal action represents an effort to hold the company accountable for environmental contamination at defense sites. The chemicals have raised concerns about potential health impacts on service members, base workers, and surrounding communities.

3M manufactured aqueous film-forming foams containing PFAS that were deployed at numerous Australian military facilities. The government contends the company knew about risks associated with these chemicals but failed to disclose that information to users and regulators.

The $1.4 billion figure reflects Australia's assessment of cleanup costs, environmental damage, and other impacts stemming from PFAS contamination at the affected sites. The lawsuit seeks to recover funds the government says it will need to address the contamination.

Similar legal battles over PFAS contamination have unfolded in other countries, particularly in the United States, where 3M and other manufacturers have faced thousands of lawsuits. The chemical industry has come under increasing scrutiny as research continues to emerge about the persistence and potential health effects of these compounds.

The case will proceed through Australian courts, where the government will need to prove its allegations that 3M withheld critical safety information about the products used at military bases.

cards.headline: Google Engineer Charged with $1.2 Million Insider Trading on Polymarket
cards.teaser: Federal prosecutors charged a Google employee with using confidential company information to profit from bets placed on the prediction market platform.
cards.body:
Original Card (Unchanged)

The Department of Justice charged a Google engineer with insider trading after he allegedly made $1.2 million through bets on Polymarket, a platform where users wager on future events. Prosecutors say the employee operated under the username AlphaRaccoon.

The case involves allegations that the engineer used internal Google data about search terms to place informed bets on the prediction market. Authorities say he leveraged confidential information available through his position at the company to gain an unfair advantage over other Polymarket users.

---

Note: The sources confirm the core facts but provide limited additional confirmed details beyond what's already in the original card. The sources mention the engineer's name (Michele Spagnuolo) and that bets were related to Google's 2025 Year in Search campaign, but without more specifics about charges or outcomes, I'm returning the original text as it accurately reflects the confirmed reporting.

cards.headline: European Union Fines Temu $230 Million for Selling Unsafe Products
cards.teaser: The European Commission penalized the Chinese e-commerce platform for offering baby toys and other items that could harm consumers.
cards.body:
Temu faces a fine exceeding $230 million from European Union regulators for selling products deemed unsafe for consumers. The European Commission identified baby toys among the items that raised safety concerns.

The penalty targets the Chinese e-commerce platform's sale of goods that the commission determined could cause harm to buyers. The fine represents one of the EU's enforcement actions against online marketplaces over product safety standards.

cards.headline: Oil Prices Rise After US Shoots Down Iranian Drones
cards.teaser: Oil markets reacted to renewed military tensions after the United States said it intercepted four Iranian attack drones.
cards.body:
Oil prices increased following a US military announcement that it shot down four Iranian attack drones. The incident occurred despite ongoing peace talks between the two countries, raising concerns about the stability of negotiations aimed at ending hostilities in the region.

Energy markets responded to the escalation with price increases, reflecting concerns about potential disruptions to Middle Eastern oil supplies. The military action demonstrated the fragile state of US-Iran relations even as diplomatic efforts continued.

cards.headline: Legal Protections May Not Cover Genetic Information as Predictive Medicine Advances
cards.teaser: Legal scholars warn that federal anti-discrimination guidelines may be outdated as genetic testing becomes more common in medicine.
cards.body:
The growth of genetic scoring and predictive medicine has raised questions about whether current anti-discrimination laws adequately protect genetic information. Legal experts caution that federal guidelines written decades ago may not address modern uses of DNA data.

The concern centers on potential conflicts between genetic testing and employment. As medical technology advances and genetic information becomes more predictive of health outcomes, scholars warn existing legal frameworks may not prevent discrimination based on genetic profiles.

cards.headline: UK Risks Lost Generation as Youth Unemployment Projected to Rise
cards.teaser: A new report projects 1.25 million young people aged 16 to 24 will be out of work, education, or training by 2031 without intervention.
cards.body:
One in six young people in the UK will not be working or in training within five years without policy changes, according to a new report. The analysis forecasts that 1.25 million people aged 16 to 24 will fall into this category by 2031.

The report warns that the UK faces the risk of a lost generation if current trends continue. The projection reflects growing numbers of young adults who are neither employed nor participating in education or job training programs.

---

Note: The additional source material provided relates to different stories (energy price caps and migrant detention centres) and does not contain information about youth unemployment. The original card text has been returned unchanged.

cards.headline: Ousted BP Chairman Denies Allegations About His Conduct
cards.teaser: Albert Manifold rejected what he called lies about his behavior during his tenure at the energy company.
cards.body:
Former BP chairman Albert Manifold has denied allegations about his conduct while leading the company, calling them "lies." He argued that people making accusations should not be allowed to remain anonymous and should identify themselves publicly.

Manifold was recently removed from his position as chairman. Reports have suggested bullying and overbearing behaviour played a role in his abrupt dismissal, though BP has declined to comment on the specific reasons behind his removal.

hero.headline: Google engineer charged with insider trading after earning $1.2 million on Polymarket
hero.body:
Federal authorities have charged a Google engineer with insider trading after the employee earned $1.2 million through wagers on the prediction market platform Polymarket.

The complaint alleges the engineer placed bets totaling over $2.7 million on wagers connected to Google's 2025 Year in Search campaign. The charges suggest the employee used non-public information about the company's annual search trends summary to profit on the betting platform.

Polymarket operates as a prediction market where users can wager on the outcomes of future events, ranging from political elections to corporate announcements. The platform has grown in popularity as a tool for forecasting, but it has also raised regulatory concerns about potential misuse of insider information.

The case represents one of the first major insider trading prosecutions involving prediction markets rather than traditional stock trading. Federal prosecutors appear to be signaling that insider trading laws apply equally to cryptocurrency-based betting platforms as they do to conventional securities markets.

Google has not yet commented publicly on the charges against its employee. The engineer's name was not provided in the available information about the complaint.

Insider trading occurs when someone trades or bets using material non-public information that could affect the value of a security or, in this case, the outcome of a prediction market. Federal law prohibits such activity because it undermines fair markets and gives unfair advantages to those with access to confidential information.

The charges come as regulators have increased scrutiny of prediction markets and their potential for abuse. The Commodity Futures Trading Commission has previously raised questions about whether certain prediction markets should be regulated as derivatives exchanges.

The size of the alleged profit, at $1.2 million, represents a substantial return on information that should have remained confidential within Google. Prosecutors will need to prove the engineer had access to non-public information about the Year in Search campaign and used that information to place the bets.

cards.headline: Valve increases Steam Deck prices by over 40 percent
cards.teaser: Valve has raised Steam Deck prices by more than 40 percent, with some models increasing by as much as $300.
cards.body:
Valve has raised Steam Deck prices significantly, with the 512GB OLED model jumping to $789 from $549, and the 1TB model now priced at $949, up from $649. The company cited rising component costs as the reason for the increases.

The price hikes coincide with the Steam Deck's return to stock after an extended period of unavailability. Both OLED models are currently available for purchase on Steam with estimated delivery dates listed.

cards.headline: Australia sues 3M over contamination from firefighting foam chemicals
cards.teaser: The Australian government has filed a lawsuit against 3M seeking A$2 billion over contamination at defense sites from firefighting foam.
cards.body:
The Australian government has filed its largest ever legal case against 3M, seeking A$2 billion in damages over contamination at defence sites caused by firefighting foam chemicals. The lawsuit centres on PFAS, commonly known as "forever chemicals" because they persist indefinitely in the environment.

PFAS were used in firefighting foam at military and defence installations. The chemicals have been linked to health concerns, prompting the government action against the US manufacturer.

cards.headline: Google AI struggles with spelling and basic word definitions
cards.teaser: Google's AI systems are having difficulty spelling the company's own name and defining basic words like disregard, stop, and ignore.
cards.body:
Google's artificial intelligence tools are experiencing problems with fundamental language tasks, including spelling the word Google and defining common terms. The AI Overview feature has particularly struggled with words such as disregard, stop, and ignore.

Users across the internet have noted the issues, with many questioning whether the problems indicate deeper flaws in the AI systems. The spelling and definition errors have prompted some to consider whether competing services like Microsoft might offer more reliable alternatives.

cards.headline: Forecasters predict below-average Atlantic hurricane season
cards.teaser: Meteorologists expect fewer hurricanes in the Atlantic this year due to El Niño, but warn residents should still prepare.
cards.body:
Forecasters are predicting a below-average hurricane season for the Atlantic Ocean, with El Niño conditions expected to reduce storm formation. The climate pattern typically suppresses hurricane development in the Atlantic basin.

Despite the more favorable forecast, meteorologists emphasized that residents in hurricane-prone areas should not become complacent. Even below-average seasons can produce destructive storms, and preparedness remains essential for coastal communities.

cards.headline: NASA spacecraft captures images of Mars during flyby
cards.teaser: NASA's Psyche spacecraft photographed Mars while passing the planet on its journey to study a distant asteroid.
cards.body:
NASA's Psyche mission captured detailed photographs of Mars during a flyby of the red planet. The spacecraft is en route to study a far-off asteroid but passed close enough to Mars to take images.

The probe recorded views of a crescent Mars and created a timelapse of the planet. The flyby represents a bonus scientific opportunity for a mission primarily focused on reaching and studying an asteroid in the outer solar system.

cards.headline: Vertu launches AI-powered foldable phone for executives starting at $6,880
cards.teaser: Luxury phone maker Vertu has released a foldable device aimed at CEOs, featuring AI agent workflows and enterprise integrations.
cards.body:
Vertu has launched a new AI-powered foldable smartphone aimed at corporate executives, starting at $6,880. The device is built on the open-source Hermes project and integrates AI-agent workflows with enterprise software tools, allowing business leaders to manage company operations from their mobile device.

The phone features ultra-premium luxury finishes and materials, positioning it among the market's most expensive smartphones. Its design caters to executives seeking advanced AI capabilities combined with high-end craftsmanship and enterprise functionality.

hero.headline: Steve Clarke extends Scotland contract through 2030 World Cup
hero.body:
Scotland manager Steve Clarke has signed a new contract extension that will keep him in the role through the 2030 World Cup and the 2028 European Championship.

The deal represents a significant commitment from the Scottish Football Association to Clarke, who has led the national team since 2019. Under his management, Scotland ended a 23-year absence from major tournaments by qualifying for Euro 2020. The extended agreement ensures continuity in Scottish football leadership across multiple tournament cycles.

Clarke will oversee qualification campaigns for the 2028 Euros and the 2030 World Cup. Scotland has not featured in a World Cup since 1998, when they competed in France. The contract extension gives Clarke the opportunity to end that absence and guide the nation back to the global stage.

The decision to extend Clarke's terms comes at a pivotal moment in his tenure. There has been tension between the manager and some sections of the support, particularly regarding Scotland's performances at recent European Championships. Clarke previously expressed frustration about the absence of a new contract offer, indicating it was a concern heading into the World Cup qualification process.

The timing of the agreement was significant. The Scottish Football Association faced criticism for not resolving Clarke's future immediately after Scotland qualified for the World Cup. Delaying the decision risked creating a distraction during the tournament itself.

The 2028 European Championship will take place across the United Kingdom and Republic of Ireland. Scotland's Hampden Park stadium in Glasgow is among the proposed venues, potentially providing home advantage during the competition.

The 2030 World Cup will adopt an unprecedented format, taking place across multiple continents including Spain, Portugal, Morocco, Uruguay, Argentina, and Paraguay. The tournament marks the centenary of the first World Cup, which was held in Uruguay in 1930.

Clarke has overseen Scotland's qualification for three major tournaments during his seven years in charge. His tenure has transformed the perception of Scottish football internationally, moving the team away from years of irrelevance. However, the performances at recent tournaments have not always met supporter expectations, creating a complex relationship between the manager and sections of the fanbase.

Despite criticism from some quarters, there remains no obvious alternative candidate for the position. The Scottish Football Association's decision to commit to Clarke through multiple tournament cycles suggests confidence in his ability to continue developing the team.

The financial terms of the contract extension have not been disclosed. The agreement ranks among the longer-term commitments given to national team managers in European football.

cards.headline: Arsenal and PSG prepare for Champions League final
cards.teaser: Paris St-Germain holds a potential advantage over Arsenal ahead of Saturday's Champions League final.
cards.body:
Paris St-Germain and Arsenal will compete in the Champions League final on Saturday. For Arsenal, this represents their first appearance in the competition's final since 2006—a 20-year absence from European football's biggest club match.

PSG holds a significant advantage in European experience, with their squad having accumulated roughly 7,000 more minutes in Champions League competition than their English opponents. Arsenal's players have spoken about what winning the trophy would mean to them as the team prepares for the encounter.

cards.headline: Crystal Palace awaits Iraola decision with Lampard as backup option
cards.teaser: Crystal Palace is waiting for a response from Andoni Iraola about their managerial vacancy.
cards.body:
Crystal Palace are awaiting Andoni Iraola's response after approaching the manager about their vacant position. Frank Lampard, who currently manages Coventry, is being considered as a backup option should Iraola decline the role.

The managerial search comes after Palace's Conference League triumph, which secured them automatic qualification for next season's Europa League.

cards.headline: Bristol Bears coach Pat Lam defends position after record 94-33 loss
cards.teaser: Pat Lam says he remains the right person to lead Bristol Bears despite a historic defeat.
cards.body:
Bristol Bears coach Pat Lam has defended his position following a record 94-33 defeat to Northampton Saints. The loss represents the heaviest defeat in the club's history.

Despite the heavy margin of loss, Lam remains confident in his ability to lead the team and believes he is still the right person for the job.

cards.headline: Sophie Ecclestone targets T20 World Cup after mental health challenges
cards.teaser: England spinner Sophie Ecclestone has opened up about her mental health struggles and World Cup ambitions.
cards.body:
England spinner Sophie Ecclestone has opened up about battling mental health struggles during her cricket career. She has also addressed the criticism she received over her fitness levels.

Ecclestone views a T20 World Cup victory as a significant objective that would help set things right as she continues representing England at international level.

cards.headline: Republic of Ireland defender Coleman questions Israel fixture protocols
cards.teaser: Seamus Coleman says players should not be put in position to answer questions about facing Israel.
cards.body:
Republic of Ireland defender Seamus Coleman has criticized the handling of the Israel fixture controversy, insisting that players should not be responsible for addressing such questions. Coleman said the situation should never have reached the squad level.

Ireland faces Israel in upcoming Nations League matches, but the fixture has prompted debate about whether the team should participate.

cards.headline: Naomi Osaka debuts bold fashion at French Open
cards.teaser: Tennis player Naomi Osaka wore an Eiffel Tower inspired outfit at the French Open in Paris.
cards.body:
Naomi Osaka appeared at the French Open wearing a distinctive outfit that combined couture fashion with tennis attire. The ensemble included an ivory train and gold bomber jacket.

The outfit drew inspiration from the Eiffel Tower, fitting the Parisian location of the tournament. Osaka has chosen bold fashion statements for her French Open campaign following previous criticism of her fashion show appearances.

hero.headline: Insiders describe toxic culture at UK reality show after rape allegations
hero.body:
Insiders at the UK reality show Married at First Sight have described a toxic culture at the program, according to new reports. The revelations follow earlier accounts from two women who told the BBC they had been raped while participating in the Channel 4 show.

The insider accounts detail what sources characterized as an unhealthy focus on sex within the production environment. Channel 4 broadcasts the British version of the international franchise, which pairs strangers who marry upon first meeting and document their relationships.

The two women who previously spoke to the BBC described separate incidents of rape that they say occurred during their time on the show. Their accounts prompted the latest wave of scrutiny into the program's internal practices and duty of care protocols.

Reality television programs in the UK have faced increased examination regarding participant welfare in recent years. Regulators and broadcasters have implemented various safeguarding measures, though critics argue protections remain inadequate for people placed in high-pressure filming environments.

The Married at First Sight franchise operates in multiple countries, with each version produced independently. The UK edition has run for multiple seasons and regularly draws significant viewership on Channel 4.

Channel 4 has not publicly responded to the latest insider allegations about the show's culture. The network previously stated it takes participant welfare seriously when the initial rape allegations became public.

The BBC reporting that brought forward the two women's accounts has sparked broader conversations about accountability in reality television production. Industry observers note that participants often sign extensive contracts that can limit their ability to speak publicly about their experiences.

The allegations come during a period of heightened attention to safeguarding practices across British television. Several high-profile cases involving reality programming have led to calls for stricter industry standards and independent oversight of participant care.

cards.headline: BBC News receives Emmy for Myanmar earthquake coverage
cards.teaser: The network's reporting on the devastating earthquake won recognition at an awards ceremony in New York.
cards.body: BBC News won an Emmy Award for its coverage of the Myanmar earthquake at a ceremony held in New York on Wednesday. The award recognized the network's reports and live updates documenting the devastating tremor that struck the country, causing significant destruction and casualties in Myanmar.

cards.headline: Multiple artists withdraw from government-sponsored Freedom 250 concert
cards.teaser: Young MC and Morris Day pulled out of the Washington event after learning of its Trump administration backing.
cards.body:
Rapper Young MC has withdrawn from the Freedom 250 concert series, becoming the second artist to exit the Trump administration-backed festival celebrating America's 250th birthday on the National Mall in Washington. His departure followed Morris Day's announcement that he and the Time would not participate in the event.

Young MC cited a lack of transparency, stating that artists were not informed about the political involvement behind the concert series. C+C Music Factory is currently deciding whether to continue its involvement with the festival.

cards.headline: Cannes winners acquired by Indian distributor before festival opened
cards.teaser: Impact Films secured distribution rights for both the Palme d'Or and Grand Prix winners for South Asia.
cards.body:
Impact Films acquired distribution rights for both the Palme d'Or winner and Grand Prix winner from the Cannes Film Festival before the event began. The Indian company secured Cristian Mungiu's Fjord and Andrei Zvyagintsev's Minotaur for South Asian distribution.

Fjord marks Mungiu's first film shot outside Romania. Impact Films obtained the Palme d'Or winner from Goodfellas, completing what the company described as a rare double acquisition of the festival's top prizes.

cards.headline: House of the Dragon season premiere set to open Italian film festival
cards.teaser: The first episode of season three will debut at the Taormina Film Festival with cast members in attendance.
cards.body:
The Italian premiere of House of the Dragon's third season will open the Taormina Film Festival, running June 10-14 in Sicily. HBO's series will debut its first episode at the festival screening.

Cast members Steve Toussaint, Harry Collett, and Bethany Antonia are scheduled to attend the premiere. Toussaint plays Lord Corlys Velaryon, Collett portrays Jacaerys Velaryon, and Antonia appears as Baela Targaryen in the series.

cards.headline: Sherlock villain Moriarty to get his own drama series
cards.teaser: Fremantle and Archery Pictures are developing a show centered on Professor James Moriarty.
cards.body:
Fremantle and Archery Pictures are developing a drama series centered on Professor James Moriarty, the criminal mastermind from Arthur Conan Doyle's Sherlock Holmes stories. Rather than focusing on the detective himself, this new series will place the villain at the center of the narrative.

The project reflects a shift in how producers are approaching Holmes material. With numerous adaptations of the famous detective already produced for television, turning attention to Moriarty offers a fresh angle on Conan Doyle's enduring source material.

cards.headline: Hong Kong drama Afterpiece to open Shanghai Film Festival
cards.teaser: The film about a paralyzed stage director will have its world premiere at the festival in June.
cards.body:
Afterpiece will world premiere as the opening film of the 28th Shanghai International Film Festival, running June 12-21. The Hong Kong drama was produced by Derek Yee and directed by debut filmmaker Keane T.K. Wong.

The film follows Owen, a stage director who once received acclaim but has spent more than a decade unable to create new work. The production marks Wong's first feature as a director.

hero.headline: CEO confidence drops as Iran war continues
hero.teaser: Business leaders at major companies grew more pessimistic in the second quarter as the Iran conflict extended.
hero.body:
CEO confidence fell 12 points in the second quarter, dropping to 47 on a scale where below 50 indicates more negative than positive sentiment, according to a survey by The Conference Board and The Business Council. The decline reflects ongoing uncertainty as the Iran war continues without resolution.

The conflict has already begun affecting households and businesses. Energy prices have risen significantly due to the war's impact, with typical household energy bills increasing by £221 annually under new price cap regulations. Meanwhile, military escalations continue, with Israel intensifying attacks against Hezbollah in Lebanon and U.S. forces striking Iranian targets as diplomatic negotiations for a ceasefire remain ongoing.

cards.headline: White working-class voters turn against Trump
cards.teaser: White voters without college degrees who backed Trump's reelection now disapprove of his job performance.
cards.body:
White voters without college degrees have shifted to net-negative approval of President Trump's job performance, marking a reversal for a demographic that voted to reelect him by a large margin. The group was a core part of Trump's electoral coalition.

The shift represents a significant change in support from a voter bloc that has historically backed Trump by wide margins. The drop in approval comes as multiple challenges face the administration.

cards.headline: Cornyn loses Texas primary to Paxton in blowout
cards.teaser: Attorney General Ken Paxton defeated longtime Sen. John Cornyn in the Texas Republican Senate primary.
cards.body:
Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton won the Republican Senate primary against Sen. John Cornyn in a lopsided result that energized President Trump and the MAGA base. The loss dealt a major blow to Senate GOP leaders who had invested tens of millions of dollars in supporting Cornyn.

The outcome puts new pressure on Senate Majority Leader John Thune and other Senate Republicans to align more closely with Trump's agenda. Republican strategists described the result as giving Trump increased leverage over the Senate Republican conference heading into the general election.

cards.headline: Democrats see Texas Senate seat as pickup opportunity with Paxton nomination
cards.teaser: Democrats believe Ken Paxton's primary victory makes the Texas Senate seat competitive in November.
cards.body:
Democrats say the Texas Senate seat is competitive and potentially winnable after Ken Paxton's victory in the Republican primary. The party's candidate is state Rep. James Talarico, who will face Paxton in the general election.

Paxton's win exhilarated the MAGA base but also energized Democrats, who view the race as one of their best pickup opportunities of the 2026 cycle. Latino voters are expected to play a key role in the outcome, with Democrats focusing on this demographic as part of their strategy to flip the seat.

cards.headline: Ebola outbreak in Congo outpaces containment efforts
cards.teaser: An Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo is spreading faster than health workers can contain it.
cards.body:
An Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo is spreading faster than containment efforts can manage, according to the World Health Organization. The WHO's director-general warned that the epidemic is outpacing response operations and urged neighboring countries to take immediate action to prevent the disease from crossing borders.

The Trump administration is building a quarantine and treatment center in Kenya for Americans exposed to the virus, rather than allowing them to return to the United States. Some health experts have criticized this approach, arguing that preventing Americans from coming home may hinder treatment efforts.

cards.headline: Buttigieg leads early 2028 Democratic primary polling
cards.teaser: Former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg tops a hypothetical Democratic presidential field for 2028.
cards.body:
Pete Buttigieg leads a crowded field of potential Democratic presidential candidates with 18 percent support in an Emerson College Polling survey released Thursday. California Gov. Gavin Newsom came in second place with 16 percent.

The polling reflects the Democratic Party's search for a new direction after losses in 2024. Buttigieg served as Transportation Secretary in the previous administration before leaving the post.

cards.headline: Vance and Rubio tied in 2028 Republican primary polling
cards.teaser: Vice President Vance and Secretary of State Rubio are nearly tied in early polling for the 2028 GOP nomination.
